correctness.rationale: Even-power Parseval makes every convolution coefficient nonnegative after taking absolute amplitudes; equality constraints on the lattice of additive relations recover phases e^{i(theta+lambda_j t0)} once all amplitudes are positive. Global maximizing amplitudes converge to the unique flat l2 Cauchy-Schwarz vector by K_p→sqrt m, so a uniform C² parameter Laplace expansion applies near exactly g equal-phase peaks of curvature V(a). The tangent Hessian of log sum a at the flat vector is -I; a small 1/p variance gradient gives unique positive optimizer and stated drift. Independent exact-convolution numerical optimization of Lambda={0,1,3} at p=20,40,80 has coefficient drift discrepancy 0.00138,0.000328,0.0000795 consistent with O(p^-2); finite tests do not establish p→infty uniqueness.

originality.rationale: Prior Hardy–Littlewood majorant theory supplies the even-integer nonnegative-amplitude reduction. The fully inspected October 11 sharp L2→L6 theorem on support {0,1,3} gives the exact *single p=6* optimizer (nonuniform) but not arbitrary supports and growing exponent. Ganzburg–Saucedo–Tikhonov use derivative/smoothness-order limits, Ganzburg 2019 varies spectral bandwidth, and Jaming–Kellay–Saba study lower L1 estimates. No inspected theorem implies the high-p first correction and its full optimal amplitude drift.
residual_risks: Abstract general parameter-dependent Laplace optimization could reproduce the formula under different terminology; it was not established in the inspected sharp Fourier-norm literature. Unique phase classification uses sufficiently large even p, not other exponents.

value.rationale: A universal asymptotic geometry-of-aperture result for the natural sharp Fourier synthesis operator norm; frequencies far from mean lose amplitude by a computable first-order amount, with a full optimizer phase class rather than only a scalar fixed-vector Laplace approximation.

final_claim: For fixed m>=2 distinct integer frequencies Lambda and Haar-circle L^p, as even p→infty the sharp coefficient-l2 to L^p log norm is 0.5log m-(log p)/(2p)+(1/p)log[g/sqrt(2pi V)]+O_Lambda(p^-2); maximizing positive magnitudes are unique and equal 1/sqrt m-((lambda_j-mu)^2-V)/(2p sqrt m V)+O(p^-2); all complex maximizers are global-phase/translation-phase equivalents.
limitations: Fixed finite one-dimensional distinct integer frequencies and Haar normalized L^p; all p sufficiently large even. No uniformity in growing Lambda, nor exact phase rigidity at odd/non-even p.
